svg.aria-label: A transform coder in four steps on one synthetic 8 by 8 block, then decoded. Step 1, the block: pixel values 100 + 6x + 4y, from 100 at top left to 170 at bottom right, level-shifted by −128. Step 2, the forward DCT of ITU-T T.81: 64 coefficients, 9 of them nonzero to one decimal, all in row 0 or column 0: 56.0, −109.3, −11.4, −3.4 and −0.9 along the first row, −72.9, −7.6, −2.3 and −0.6 down the first column. Step 3, quantisation: each coefficient is divided by its entry in T.81 Table K.1 and rounded; 5 survive (4, −10 and −1 in the first row, −6 and −1 in the first column) and the four high-frequency ones, −3.4, −0.9, −2.3 and −0.6, become 0, so 59 of 64 values are zero. Worked examples: 56.0 ÷ 16 = 3.5 rounds to 4, a tie rounded away from zero; −109.3 ÷ 11 ≈ −9.94 rounds to −10, decoded as −110; −3.4 ÷ 40 ≈ −0.085 rounds to 0 and is gone. Step 4, entropy coding: in zig-zag order the values are 4, −10, −6, 0, 0, 0, −1, 0, 0, −1, then 54 zeros at indices 10 to 63, passed to a Huffman or arithmetic coder. Step 5, decoding: multiply by the table, inverse DCT, add 128; the reconstructed block differs from the original by at most 3 levels, a PSNR of 44.26 dB. Green cells are nonzero after quantisation, red cells are nonzero coefficients rounded to zero, white cells are zero; thin blue arrows carry the data from step to step.
svg.text: 9 nonzero, all in row 0 or column 0
a tie, rounded away from zero
gone: no decoder can restore it
